full_judgment:
2. In this case the plaintiffs managed to get an ex-parte decree from the Munsif, Fist Court, Sylhet in respect of scheduled waqf property. The learned Munsif, decreed the suit ex-parte without any observation as to the necessity of the Waqf Estate for settling the Waqf property and that Mvi. Abdur Rashid Chowdhury, Manager, was at all legally authorised to settle such huge waqf property. 

 6. Mr. Shakhawat Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, submits that in an application under order IX Rule 13 of C.P.C., the Court will consider as to whether the notice upon the defendants were duly served or not or as to whether the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause in appearing before the trial Court when the case was called for hearing, the learned Courts below found answer in favour of respondents and rightly held that the instant Miscellaneous case was hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 11. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of. The ex-parte decree dated 12.02.1968 passed in Title Suit No.216 of 1968 by the learned Munsif, First Court, Sylhet Sadar is hereby set aside. The trial Court should dispose of the suit expeditiously prefer-able within one year from the date of communication of this order upon allowing the defendants to submit their written statement and also allowing the parties to adduce evidence in support of their respective cases. The trial Court is also directed to serve notice upon the defendants afresh.
